title: Expiration Notice Protection for Re-Contract Starting Rates — Residential Natural Gas Supply
content:
When a Residential Natural Gas Supply agreement has rolled over and the customer re-contracts, the timing of the two expiration notices issued for the expired term decides the re-contract starting rate, the per-therm rate from which the re-contract rate is figured.

## Compliance of each notice

A notice is compliant under the gas expiration notice timing: the initial renewal notice when its notice date falls no earlier than 60 and no later than 45 calendar days before the contract end date it refers to, and the final options notice when its notice date falls no later than 30 calendar days before that date and after the initial renewal notice. These figures — 60, 45 and 30 calendar days — are the same on every Residential Natural Gas Supply plan.

## The protection rule

When the initial renewal notice and the final options notice were both non-compliant, the re-contract starting rate is the held expiring rate now carried as the agreement's contract rate; when exactly one of the two notices was non-compliant, the re-contract starting rate is the average of the final options notice's renewal rate and the held expiring rate, rounded half up to four decimal places; when both notices were compliant, the re-contract starting rate is the final options notice's renewal rate.

| Initial renewal notice | Final options notice | Re-contract starting rate |
|---|---|---|
| non-compliant | non-compliant | the held expiring rate (the agreement's contract rate) |
| compliant | non-compliant | average of the final options notice's renewal rate and the held expiring rate, rounded half up to four decimal places |
| non-compliant | compliant | average of the final options notice's renewal rate and the held expiring rate, rounded half up to four decimal places |
| compliant | compliant | the final options notice's renewal rate |

The records read are the most recent initial renewal notice and the most recent final options notice on the agreement — each with its notice date and the contract end date it refers to — and the contract rate on the agreement record.

## Worked cases (hypothetical notices; contract end date 30 September)

- **Notice dates.** An initial renewal notice dated 1 August is 60 days before and compliant; one dated 31 July (61 days) or 17 August (44 days) is not. With the initial notice dated 5 August, a final options notice dated 31 August (30 days before) is compliant; one dated 1 September (29 days) is not.
- **Exactly one non-compliant.** Final options notice renewal rate 0.8125, held expiring rate 0.7360: the two total 1.5485, half of which is 0.77425, rounded half up to 0.7743.
- **Both non-compliant.** Held expiring rate 0.7360: the starting rate is 0.7360.
- **Both compliant.** The starting rate is the renewal rate 0.8125.
